newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil continues to get better terms for debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil continues to get better terms for debt.

text.p: The terms offered to Brazil on its external debt continued to improve significantly in the first quarter of 1997, the Central Bank said.

The bank said in a statement that the average maturity on the 71 Brazilian public and private sector issues in January to March was 8.1 years, compared with 7.7 years in the last quarter of 1996 and 6.6 years in the first quarter of last year.
It said the average spread over U.S. Treasuries narrowed to 352 basis points from 407 basis points and 462 basis points respectively.
The average global cost of the bonds was equivalent to 9.77 percent a year versus 10.22 percent in the last quarter and 10.52 percent in the first quarter of 1996.
The government won an average maturity of 7.5 years and average spread of 229 basis points over Treasuries for its two issues.

The private non-financial sector scored an average maturity of 8.5 years and spread of 394 basis points. The private financial sector had an average maturity of 7.2 years and spread of 378 basis points, the Central Bank said.
